page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core, and includes 3780 GB of local SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong CPU performance, scoring 2110.0 in Geekbench single-core and 16603.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. It also achieves a strong static web serving throughput of 43.34 GB/sec and performs well in text generation for small language models, reaching 296.69 tokens/sec. However, memory performance presents a notable tradeoff, with the PassMark memory score rated as weak at 1572.37. Additionally, while the CPU's AMX instructions assist with smaller AI workloads, text generation for large 70B models is poor, yielding only 2.45 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-32ds_v6 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with a large local storage allocation on a dedicated CPU profile. This makes it a qualitatively efficient choice for memory-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration but benefit from high-speed local scratch space. Appropriate workloads include large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics, enterprise application hosting, and software compilation.
